1000445.etyen:
A surname variant of Næss, with ⟨e⟩ for ⟨æ⟩. Ultimately from Norwegian farm names and places named Nes or traditionally spelled Næs, from the common noun nes (“headland, point of land”), from Old Norse nes (“headland, promontory”), from Proto-Germanic *nasją (“headland, cape”), itself derived from Proto-Germanic *nasō (“nose”).
Compare Danish Næs, Swedish Näs and English Ness (“surname and place-name element”).

1000957.etyen:
Deverbal from gratulere (“to congratulate”), using its present tense as a congratulatory formula. The noun is a nominalization of the same form.
The underlying verb comes from Latin grātulārī (“to congratulate”), derived from Latin grātus (“pleasing, welcome; grateful”), from Proto-Italic *gʷrātos (“grateful”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷr̥Htós (“praised”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH- (“to welcome, praise”).

1001213.etyen:
Borrowed from Swedish IKEA, a lexicalized acronym formed from the initial letters of Ingvar Kamprad, Elmtaryd and Agunnaryd. It is named after Swedish entrepreneur Ingvar Kamprad, while the final two initials refer to the farm where he grew up and the parish and nearby village. Elmtaryd is now spelled Älmtaryd. The trading company was registered on 28 July 1943.

The interjection guri derives from the female given name Guri, continuing Old Norse Guðríðr.
